problems.title: A root of a large power
problems.question: Simplify sixteenth-root(8¹²).
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the wording permits more than one case.
steps: Since 8=2³, the value is 2^(9/4), the listed answer.

problems.title: Union probability for independent events
problems.question: Which union-probability formula holds for all independent A,B?
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the wording permits more than one case.
formulas: $P(A\cup B)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A\cap B)$; independence gives $P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)$.
steps: Substituting the product yields P(A∪B)=P(A)+P(B)−P(A)P(B).

problems.title: Union probability for incompatible events
problems.question: Which union-probability formula holds for all mutually exclusive A,B?
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the wording permits more than one case.
formulas: Mutual exclusivity means $A\cap B=\varnothing$, hence $P(A\cap B)=0$.
steps: The addition rule reduces to P(A∪B)=P(A)+P(B). This need not equal 1.

problems.title: Parallelogram area from two altitudes
problems.question: Two altitudes from a parallelogram vertex have lengths 2,3 and angle α between them. Find its area.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the wording permits more than one case.
formulas: If side lengths are u,v and included angle θ, then altitudes are u sinθ,v sinθ and area $S=uv\sin\theta$.
steps: Their product is 6=uv sin²θ=S sinθ. Perpendicularity preserves sine of the angle, so sinα=sinθ.
Therefore S=6/sinα.

problems.title: A zero dot product despite radical components
problems.question: Find the angle between a=(cube-root(5⁷),2^(5/6)) and b=(−sixth-root(2⁵),5^(7/3)).
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the wording permits more than one case.
formulas: Write the components as $a=(u,v)$ and $b=(-v,u)$.
steps: Here u=5^(7/3),v=2^(5/6), both nonzero. The dot product is −uv+vu=0, so the vectors are perpendicular.

problems.title: Mode, median and mean from frequencies
problems.question: Ten die results have counts 1,2,3,4,0,0 for scores 1,…,6. Find mode+median+mean.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the wording permits more than one case.
formulas: Mean = weighted sum/count; median is the mean of the fifth and sixth sorted scores.
steps: Mode=4, the most frequent score. Both middle observations are 3, so median=3.

problems.title: Classify an alternating geometric sequence
problems.question: Classify aₙ=(−2)ⁿ among increasing,decreasing,bounded,constant,arithmetic,or none.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the wording permits more than one case.
formulas: Consecutive ratio is −2, and magnitudes grow without bound.
steps: The terms −2,4,−8,16,… alternate signs, so they are neither increasing nor decreasing. They are unbounded and nonconstant, with nonconstant successive differences.
It is geometric, which is not one of the specific listed classifications. Thus choose “all previous answers are false.”
problems.answer: None of the listed specific classifications.

problems.title: Range of a rational linear fraction
problems.question: Find the range of (3x−4)/(5x−6).
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the wording permits more than one case.
formulas: Solve $y=(3x-4)/(5x-6)$ for x.
steps: (5y−3)x=6y−4. At y=3/5 this is impossible; otherwise x=(6y−4)/(5y−3), which never equals excluded x=6/5.
The range is all real numbers except 3/5.

problems.title: Total area from two diagonal triangles
problems.question: The smallest and largest of a trapezoid’s four diagonal-triangle areas are 2,3. Find total area.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the wording permits more than one case.
formulas: The other two areas are equal to the geometric mean of the base-adjacent areas.
steps: The middle areas are √(2×3)=√6 each. Total=2+3+2√6=5+2√6=(√2+√3)².

problems.title: The region between two disjoint chords is ambiguous
problems.question: A radius-2√3 disk has nonintersecting,nonparallel chords of lengths 2√6 and 6. Find its area between them.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the wording permits more than one case.
formulas: Minor segment area $=R^2(\theta-\sin\theta)/2$; the chord angles are 90° and 120°.
steps: The minor segment areas are 12(π/2−1)/2=3π−6 and 12(2π/3−√3/2)/2=4π−3√3.
If the two minor caps are disjoint, the middle region is the whole disk minus both caps: 12π−(3π−6)−(4π−3√3)=5π+6+3√3, the listed intended answer.
But a 90° cap can lie inside the 120° cap while their chord directions differ by 10°. The chords are then nonparallel and disjoint, yet the middle region is the difference of caps: π+6−3√3.
problems.answer: Intended: 5π+6+3√3. Another permitted arrangement gives π+6−3√3.
problems.note: Nonintersection and nonparallelism do not fix the relative cap arrangement. A condition selecting disjoint minor caps, or placing the centre in the middle region, is missing.

problems.title: An infinite sum four times its first two terms
problems.question: An infinite decreasing geometric progression has positive terms and total sum four times its first-two sum. Find q.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the wording permits more than one case.
steps: S=4S₂ gives 1=4(1−q²), so q²=3/4. Positivity selects q=√3/2.

problems.title: Sum all reduced thirds below ten
problems.question: Find the sum of all positive irreducible fractions below 10 with denominator 3.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the wording permits more than one case.
formulas: The fractions are n/3 with 1≤n≤29 and 3 not dividing n.
steps: Divide by 3 to get the fraction sum 100.

problems.title: Floor of a fraction and fraction of a floor
problems.question: Solve floor({x})={floor(x)} over real x.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the wording permits more than one case.
formulas: For every real x, $0\le\{x\}<1$ and floor(x) is an integer.
steps: The floor of the fractional part is zero. The fractional part of the integer floor is also zero. The equality holds for all real x.

problems.title: Sum reciprocals of altitudes
problems.question: A triangle has sides 13,14,15 and altitudes m,n,k. Find 1/m+1/n+1/k.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the wording permits more than one case.
formulas: Altitude to side a is $2S/a$; Heron gives area.
steps: Semiperimeter is 21, so S=√(21×8×7×6)=84.
The reciprocal-altitude sum is (13+14+15)/(2S)=42/168=1/4.

problems.title: Equilateral area compared with its circle annulus
problems.question: Find equilateral triangle area divided by the area between its circumcircle and incircle.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the wording permits more than one case.
formulas: Triangle area $=s^2\sqrt3/4$; $R^2=s^2/3$, $r^2=s^2/12$.
steps: The annulus area is π(R²−r²)=πs²/4. The ratio is √3/π.

problems.title: Six geometric terms versus the last three
problems.question: A six-term geometric progression’s total sum is 28 times the sum of its last three terms. Find q.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the wording permits more than one case.
formulas: If the first-three sum is T, then the last-three sum is q³T.
steps: T+q³T=28q³T. For a nonzero real geometric progression, T=b₁(1+q+q²)≠0.
Cancel T to get q³=1/27, hence q=1/3.

problems.title: Recover terms from prefix averages
problems.question: The mean of the first n terms of aₙ is 2n−1 for every positive n. Find a₁+a₄+a₇.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the wording permits more than one case.
steps: Subtracting gives aₙ=4n−3, including a₁=1. Thus a₄=13,a₇=25, and their requested sum is 1+13+25=39.

problems.title: Exactly two integers between two rational boundaries
problems.question: Find positive a for which (x−1)/(x−a)<0 has exactly two integer solutions.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the wording permits more than one case.
formulas: For a≠1, the quotient is negative strictly between its zero 1 and pole a.
steps: If 0<a<1 there are no integers between a and 1; a=1 gives no solution. For a>1, the interval is (1,a).
Exactly integers 2,3 must lie inside, so 3<a≤4. At a=4, the pole excludes 4 as required.

problems.title: Area between a median and a cevian
problems.question: ABC has area 1. N is midpoint AC; BM:MC=1:2; AM and BN meet at O. Find area OMCN.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the wording permits more than one case.
formulas: Use affine coordinates A=(0,0),B=(1,0),C=(0,1); ratios of areas are preserved.
steps: Triangle AMC has 2/3 of ABC’s area. Triangle AON has fraction det(O,N)=1/4 of ABC’s area.
Subtract: area OMCN=2/3−1/4=5/12.

problems.title: Distance to a line through two points
problems.question: Find distance from A=(−1,5) to the line through B=(3,2),C=(1,−2).
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the wording permits more than one case.
formulas: Line slope is 2; point-to-line distance $=|ax+by+c|/\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$.
steps: The line is 2x−y−4=0. At A the numerator magnitude is |−2−5−4|=11, giving distance 11/√5.

problems.title: Parabola vertices on opposite sides of a line
problems.question: For which a do vertices of y=x²−2x+a and y=x²−4x+2a lie strictly on opposite sides of y=2x?
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the wording permits more than one case.
formulas: The signed side test is y−2x.
steps: The vertices are (1,a−1) and (2,2a−4). Their signed tests are a−3 and 2a−8.
Opposite strict signs require (a−3)(a−4)<0, so 3<a<4. Endpoints put a vertex on the line and are excluded.

problems.title: A sign pattern forces a middle value positive
problems.question: A quadratic has f(50)<0,f(100)>0,f(150)>0,f(200)<0. Which listed assertion must hold?
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the wording permits more than one case.
formulas: Continuity gives roots in (50,100),(150,200); a quadratic has at most two roots.
steps: The function is positive between these two roots and negative outside, so it opens downward.
125 lies strictly between the two roots, making f(125)>0. The exact values or signs at 75 and 175 are not forced.

problems.title: A cyclic system of congruences
problems.question: For positive integers a,b,c, a≡b−5 modp,b≡c−15 modp,c≡a−7 modp. Which prime p can occur?
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the wording permits more than one case.
formulas: Add the congruences to cancel a,b,c.
steps: The result is 0≡−27 modp, so p divides 27. Its only prime divisor is 3.
The choice is attainable, for example a=1,b=6,c=21 satisfies all three congruences modulo 3.

problems.title: Shortest and longest diagonals from an odd polygon
problems.question: For odd n, the angle between a shortest and a longest diagonal from one vertex is 199 times the angle between the two longest diagonals. Which listed n is possible?
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the wording permits more than one case.
formulas: Put n=2m+1. From vertex index 0, shortest diagonals go to indices 2,2m−1; longest to m,m+1. Chord-direction differences are index differences times 180°/n.
steps: The longest-pair angle is one angular step. A shortest-to-longest angle can be m−2 or m−1 steps, depending on which diagonal of each tied length is chosen.
Thus m−2=199 or m−1=199, giving n=403 or 401. Only 403 is among the printed choices.
problems.answer: 403 among the choices; the tied-diagonal interpretations allow 401 or 403.

problems.title: Vector from a vertex to the centroid
problems.question: M is centroid of ABC,AB=x,AC=y. Express AM.
problems.idea: Use the exact formula and check whether the wording permits more than one case.
formulas: If N is midpoint BC, then $AN=(x+y)/2$ and $AM=2AN/3$.
steps: Multiplication gives AM=(x+y)/3.
